name: auto-accept-antigravity
description: Automatically accept AI agent actions (file edits, terminal commands) in VS Code — zero config, no launch flags needed
author: Kaushik Saravanan

autoAcceptAgent.enableCommandPolling.description: Poll accept commands on a timer. Turning this off leaves settings changes, event reactions, and CDP (if enabled) running.

autoAcceptAgent.pollIntervalMs.description: Interval in milliseconds between polling cycles. Lower = faster auto-acceptance but more CPU. Default: 800ms.

autoAcceptAgent.autoConfigureSettings.description: Automatically configure VS Code/Antigravity settings to skip command approval prompts.

autoAcceptAgent.interceptNotifications.description: When CDP is enabled, also click Allow buttons in the agent UI. Auto Accept does not press the primary action on unrelated VS Code notifications.

autoAcceptAgent.enableCDP.description: Enable optional CDP fallback to click approval buttons in VS Code webviews. When this is on, terminal Run buttons are clicked only after the blocked-command check. Requires the editor to be launched with --remote-debugging-port set to autoAcceptAgent.cdpPort (default 9222).

autoAcceptAgent.cdpPort.description: Localhost port for the optional CDP fallback. Only this port is contacted.

autoAcceptAgent.customButtonTexts.description: Additional button text labels to auto-click in the agent UI (for custom/localized prompts).

autoAcceptAgent.allowBlindTerminalAccept.description: DANGEROUS: Auto-approve terminal execution even when CDP is disabled and command text cannot be inspected. When false (default), terminal commands require manual approval unless CDP is connected.

autoAcceptAgent.blockedCommands.description: Commands that must not be auto-approved. A single word matches the command name only (del matches del file, not delta). Several words match that sequence (rm -rf, git push --force). If a blocked command starts, that terminal is closed and terminal auto-accept pauses for 60 seconds.
